quiz.q: What is diffusion?
quiz.a: The net movement of particles from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration

Which waste product diffuses from cells into the blood plasma to be removed by the kidneys?

quiz.a: Concentration gradient, temperature and surface area of the membrane

quiz.q: Think: why does oxygen diffuse INTO the blood in the lungs but OUT of the blood in muscles?
quiz.a: In the lungs there's more oxygen in the air than in the blood; in working muscles respiration uses it up, so there's less in the cells than in the blood

quiz.a: The diffusion of water from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane

quiz.a: Water moved into the potato cells by osmosis

quiz.a: The cylinders start at different masses, so percentages make the results fair to compare

quiz.q: Think: why would an animal cell burst in pure water, but a plant cell wouldn't?
quiz.a: Water moves in by osmosis; the plant cell's cell wall stops it bursting, but an animal cell has no cell wall

quiz.q: What is active transport?
quiz.a: Moving substances from a dilute to a more concentrated solution (against the gradient), using energy from respiration

quiz.q: Why do root hair cells need active transport?
quiz.a: The mineral ions in the soil are more dilute than inside the root cells

quiz.q: Why do cells that do lots of active transport have many mitochondria?
quiz.a: To release the energy from respiration that active transport needs

quiz.q: What is the surface area to volume ratio of a 1 cm cube?
Think: why do large animals like us need special exchange surfaces when a single-celled organism doesn't?
quiz.a: We have a small surface area to volume ratio, so diffusion through our outer surface alone would be far too slow
